critical_finding: Two independent methods improve the legal/language purity ratio by ~20%: (1) language-center projection reduces language purity from 0.975 to 0.684 while maintaining legal purity at 0.295, and (2) Erwägungen-only TF-IDF achieves the highest absolute legal purity (0.385) by focusing on legal reasoning text. However, no method achieves the target ratio >1.0 (legal purity exceeding language purity). The fundamental challenge remains: the primary geometric signal in the BGer corpus is language, not legal content.
notes: This cycle tested three approaches to the language dominance problem identified in the previous cycle: (1) linear projection to remove language-correlated embedding directions, (2) citation-graph node2vec embeddings, and (3) section-specific TF-IDF. Language projection improves the ratio but reduces absolute legal purity. Citation graph has too low coverage (5%) to meaningfully affect the 1000-decision map. Reasoning-only TF-IDF achieves the best absolute legal purity by focusing on legally substantive text. The next cycle should test whether combining language debiasing with reasoning-only text produces additive improvements, and whether legal-specific embeddings from the legal-distance lane can achieve ratio >1.0.
